study type: Cohort study (unmatched and propensity score matched)
cohort: 259,211 low-risk women with singleton pregnancies giving birth at term in the Netherlands between 2010 and 2012
finding: Among low-risk term women, intrapartum and neonatal mortality rates were comparable between midwife-led and obstetrician-led care, but midwife-led care was associated with lower intervention rates and fewer low Apgar scores.
mod_finding: Midwife-led care was associated with significantly lower rates of vaginal instrumental deliveries and intrapartum cesarean sections compared to obstetrician-led care.
